title: He didn’t hide behind his title.
paragraphs: He didn’t hide behind his title.
He rebuilt… with his daughters watching.
Because some men talk about faith.
He carried stones with his hands while raising courage in his home.
Why would God highlight that detail?

Out of all the names.
Out of all the builders.
Because something deeper was broken than walls.
And something more powerful was being rebuilt than stone.

Some of us have strong opinions…
but weak obedience.

We post verses…
but neglect our homes.

We raise hands in worship…
but don’t raise our children in truth.

We say “God first”—
but our lives whisper something else.
And deep down, you know it.
It was a symbol of shame.

Burned gates.
Collapsed walls.
A city exposed.

Of failure.
Of disobedience.
Of consequences.
And maybe that’s where you are.
Your life feels like broken stone.
Sin you renamed to feel better about.
You can get used to living in ruins.
You can call distance from God “just a season.”
You can even raise a family inside broken walls…
But God never called you to live in ruins.
And He never called you to rebuild alone.
He didn’t wait for perfect conditions.

He didn’t say:
“I’ll start when I feel ready.”
Learning what it looks like to restore what’s broken.

He didn’t just repair walls.
He modeled repentance.
Because rebuilding is not just construction.
“Next to him Shallum… ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, repaired, he and his daughters.”
Some scholars interpret this moment as culturally unusual.
Women weren’t typically recorded in construction work.
But God made sure their names weren’t erased.
Because this wasn’t just about labor.
your children are watching what you build.
You can’t pass down a faith you refuse to live.
And here’s where it cuts deep.
Because some of us are building careers…
Because rebuilding requires something we don’t like talking about:
You don’t rebuild walls while protecting the sin that broke them.
Because Shallum’s story doesn’t end with effort.
It points to a greater Builder.
Where Shallum worked with his daughters—
Jesus invites sinners into His family.
And here is the truth that changes everything:

You are not saved by rebuilding your life.
You are saved by surrendering it to Christ.
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not of works, lest anyone should boast.”
Grace empowers you to rebuild them—God’s way.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.”
So what does that mean for you?
It means your past is not your prison.
Your failure is not your identity.
Your hidden sin is not your final story.
But you must come out of hiding.
Because Jesus doesn’t rebuild fake versions of you.
Standing in front of broken walls.
Lead your home—not with perfection, but with repentance.
Because faith that is seen becomes faith that is followed.
To those who grew up watching brokenness—
You are not doomed to repeat it.
What wall in your life have you been avoiding?
And if this stirred something in you…
If you felt that conviction press against your heart—
From ruined walls to restored lives.
From hidden shame to visible grace.
From broken families to redeemed legacies.
